capture.transport: USB CoreMIDI receive source plus bounded standard-MIDI senders
capture.topology: Host destination 0 -> FM1 and FM1 source 0 -> host; both named USB Composite Device; no SysEx sent or received

initial_state.mode: Sequencer, recording armed by operator with REC
initial_state.pattern_description: operator cleared Pattern 1 with K4 Clear Pattern before arming

exact_steps: Operator cleared Pattern 1 and armed recording with REC; leftmost step flashing.
Host waited 600 ms, then sent 90 3C 00 alone as the step-advance attempt.
Host waited 600 ms, then sent 90 41 5A, waited 300 ms, sent 80 41 00.
Operator reported three lit steps with the cursor flashing on step 4.
Operator left record mode and started playback.

human_action.expected_result_before_observation: unknown whether a host can advance the step cursor without sounding a note

observations.resulting_sequencer_behaviour: The velocity-0 Note On advanced the cursor by one step and recorded a silent step. Playback emitted note 60, then note 65 333 ms later, which is two step widths, and transmitted nothing for the middle step. The loop stayed at 1500 ms.
observations.record_time_device_output: None. The FM1 transmitted nothing while recording; every captured message is either a later playback pass or was sent by the host.

record_evidence.analysis_notes: No hardware record bytes have been captured. These fixtures observe stock behaviour only and say nothing about the internal record layout.

comparison.only_intended_difference: one velocity-0 Note On inserted between the two recorded notes
comparison.differential_result: A host can insert a rest. The 2026-08-31 fixture without the velocity-0 message placed notes 60 and 65 in adjacent steps; with it they are one step apart.

notes: SEQ-001B capture. Standard channel MIDI only: no SysEx, vendor, loader, OTA or flash traffic in either direction.
Step positions are operator-reported stock step lights; playback timings are captured MIDI.
